content.content:
- **AU-35 — What a reading counts, amended (AU-11).** On stereo media the 2×2 matrix is pan ·
  fold · pick: the channel pick counts, before the base mono fold and pan. EQ and hum are not
  counted, as noise reduction and the compressor are not. Peak Normalize keeps the maximum over
  the channels (an upper bound, as it is for pan).
- **AU-36 — The drawn curve is Swift's, from the stage's own design.**
- **AU-10 — A per-media loudness cache at 10 ms, S4's format, on the cache lane after peaks.**
  `cache/loudness/<id>.bin` beside a marker `cache/loudness/<id>.complete.json`
  (`LoudnessStamp {source, version, channels, sampleRate, blocksPerSecond, oversample}`,
  `loudnessVersion` 1). The `.bin` is headerless little-endian Float32 records, one per 10 ms
  block: mono `z, tp`, stereo `zL, zR, zLR, tpL, tpR`, where `z` is the MEAN of the K-weighted
  samples squared over the block's frames (`zLR` the mean of yL·yR) and `tp` is
  max(4× Annex 2 FIR, |x|) over the block, linear. The count is `⌈duration·100⌉` from the
  marker's `source.duration`; a load checks the size, every value finite and z, tp ≥ 0 (zLR may
  be negative), and a marker of another version, another `blocksPerSecond` than 100 or another
  `oversample` than 4, or one that will not decode, reads as absent (the cache is made again).
  Frames are placed by `PeakBuckets`' rule verbatim (the file's own rate, the PTS less the MP3
  lead, `⌊f·100/rate⌋`) and the same `covers` check runs before publishing; one
  `CacheLedger.publish` writes the file then the marker, and a `mediaCacheDidChange` of kind
  `loudness` is posted on a publish and on a withdrawal. The pass runs on the lane after peaks
  and before the sync features; `loudness` answers a Bool as `peaks` does (true: nothing to
  make, current, or published), and the in-session retry (SY-11's 2 s, then 10 s) runs while
  either peaks or loudness published nothing, each attempt running loudness only after peaks
  lands and returning when both have. K-weighting is Tables 1 and 2 at exactly 48 kHz and
  libebur128's bilinear derivation from the analog prototype at any other rate; the filter state
  and the FIR's history run continuously across the file. A file whose first buffer has more
  than two channels is read again from the start with `AVNumberOfChannelsKey: 2` and stored as
  stereo; that downmix is not measured against the export's.

  what plays); the export's channel layout (a mono record's z doubled: dual mono, +3.01 LU);
  and, on stereo media, the clip's own base `mono` fold then `pan` (`AudioPanLaw.gains`) as one
  2×2 matrix over the records' `zL, zR, zLR` (mono media ignore both, as the tap does). It does
  not count noise reduction or the compressor, the volume, fades, ducks, mute or solo, or an
  enclosing nest's fold: the reading is the material's, pre-fader, as Normalize's peak is.

content.content:
# 2. The six ideas, and why the model stays simple

Six ideas do most of the work. Frame Job is built on all six.

1. **One kind of track.** Every track holds any clip — video, audio,
   still, text, shape. There are no video-vs-audio track types; an
   audio-only clip simply draws a waveform. Higher track = in front.
2. **A fixed canvas with direct manipulation.** The document has a size
   (1920×1080 by default). Clips are placed on it by dragging on the
   preview; scale, position, rotation and crop are clip properties with
   numbers in the inspector and handles on the canvas.
3. **Actions, not keyframes.** An Action is a span on a clip with an
   easing curve. You edit the property values at the *end* of the span;
   the values at the start are whatever was already in effect. There is
   no keyframe graph.
4. **Overlap is a transition.** Sliding one clip over its neighbour on
   the same track makes a transition of that length. No transition
   track, no browser to drag from.
5. **One inspector, tabbed by what the selection is.** Video / Audio /
   Text / Shape for the selected clip; Media and Document always.
6. **A small keyboard vocabulary.** ⌘T split, W/E trim to playhead,
   ⌘⌫ ripple delete, ⇧⌘F freeze frame, M marker, Space/JKL transport.

Left out: everything that only makes sense for a recording
it made itself (mouse/keyboard/touch callouts, pointer effects), templates,
publishing to YouTube/Vimeo, the stock-media library.

core/src/edit.rs:142://! | `paste` | Inserts the clips of a clipboard payload — `{"clips": […], "media": […]}`, what Copy wrote — with fresh ids, the earliest landing at `at` and the rest keeping their offsets.   in it, the power spectrum through 40 triangular HTK-mel bands from 0 to 4 kHz, `log(P·FB +
  1e-10)`, a DCT-II (unnormalised) to c0…c25. Frame f starts at sample 128·f; a file of n
  samples holds `(n − 512)/128 + 1` frames (0 under 512). Its marker `<id>.complete.json` is

## Bet 5 — Switch by Speaker, and read every audio track of a file

### Goal

A creator records a video podcast or an interview with two to four cameras and a microphone per
person. They line the files up with Synchronize Audio, select them, and choose Clip ▸ Switch by
Speaker…. Frame Job cuts to whoever is talking. It judges each microphone's speech against that
microphone's own level, so a guest's voice leaking into the host's microphone does not cut to
the host. It shows the wide shot while two people talk over each other, holds a minimum shot
length, and lets short replies ("yeah", "mm") pass without a cut. The result is one undo step:
a new Program track of ordinary clips, each a piece of one camera, over the cameras kept whole
and hidden on their own tracks. The microphones are not touched. Every cut can be rolled like
any other cut, and Clip ▸ Switch Angle re-picks the camera for one shot. Later phases add a
one-microphone mode that reads mouth movement with Vision, and an Angle Viewer that shows every
camera at once and switches while the timeline plays.

Separately, Frame Job stops reading only the first audio track of a file. An OBS recording with
the mix on track 1, the microphone on track 2 and the desktop on track 3 imports all three. A
recorder or mixer file with many channels in one track (a RØDECaster Pro II, a Zoom F-series,
a MixPre) offers each channel as its own source, and so does a wireless kit that records two
people on the left and right of one stereo track. Each track or channel can be placed as its own
clip with its own audio chain, and Detach Audio makes one linked sound clip per track. Every
measurement — the waveform, loudness, Normalize, Enhance Voice, Duck by Speech, Remove Silences,
Synchronize Audio, transcription — reads the track or channel the clip plays.

Every command has its MCP tool. No phase needs a key.

### Owner's answers applied

- **All six bets are in one road map.** This is bet 5, prefix SW; its phases are SW1–SW9b.
- **Every spec §1 non-goal is lifted.** For this bet that means multicam. The bet builds
  multicam in full: synced angles, a program track of shots, re-picking, an Angle Viewer and
  switching while playing (SW1, SW2, SW9a, SW9b). It does this without a multicam source kind:
  the shots are ordinary clips on an ordinary track (SW-10, SW-90). That is a design choice, not
  a non-goal; the owner can ask for a multicam clip instead at SW9a.
- **§11 decisions that implement a non-goal stand until a phase amends them in writing.** This
  bet amends none of them. Nest clips keep having no in point (`core/src/nest.rs:22`), there is
  still one kind of track (spec §2), and the effect vocabulary stays closed (R5-1).
- **Input Monitoring.** Not used by this bet.
- **The key rule.** Nothing in this bet uses a language model or a cloud model. Switch by
  Speaker reads the loudness cache, Silero VAD's speech cache and, in SW8, Vision face
  landmarks — all on the device, none needing a key. The Assistant can call the bet's tools on
  its own key, as it calls every tool. Transcribing a second audio track with AssemblyAI needs
  the AssemblyAI key exactly as transcribing the first does today.
- **Lead segments.** Video podcasts are the third segment, so the switch (SW1, SW2) is
  scheduled after the first phases of bets 1–4. Reading every audio track (SW3, SW4, SW5) also
  serves the first segment: screen recordists who record with OBS keep their microphone on its
  own track. The orchestrator's default lets those three phases start early, in a lane of their
  own.
- **Real use.** The owner cuts one real video per lead segment alongside bet 1. For podcasts,
  JOB-51 asks the owner to cut one real episode with Switch by Speaker once SW2 lands; the
  verdict is recorded as SW-29, the way GR-9 recorded grading's trial.
- **Build arrangement.** Every format number below is provisional ("format 38p") until its
  phase lands; the integrator renumbers on collision. Decision IDs are SW-n0…SW-n9 per phase;
  scope-level drafts are offered to CJ0 for numbering.

### How it fits the tree

At `d0661e5d`. Line counts are `wc -l`.

**A media is one file with one sound.**
- `Media` (`core/src/model.rs:162–192`, the file 570 lines) records `has_audio: bool` and
  nothing about how many audio tracks or channels the file has. Its `speech` spans
  (format 29, AU-110) belong to the file as a whole.
- `add_media` treats a path already in the list as an identity (`core/src/edit_track.rs:476`,
  the doc above it: "two entries for one path would each carry their own bookmark, thumbnails
  and peaks"). A second audio track therefore cannot be a second media row; it must be
  something a CLIP chooses.
- `Source::Media` is `{media, in, reversed}` (`core/src/model.rs:292–315`). `reversed` is the
  precedent for a fact about what a clip reads that changes neither the plan's structure nor
  the recipe.

**Every reader takes the first audio track.**
- The probe counts audio tracks and keeps only whether there is one
  (`app/Sources/MediaImporter.swift:79`, `hasAudio: !audioTracks.isEmpty` at :114).
- The builder's one synchronous track lookup answers `.first`
  (`app/Sources/CompositionBuilder.swift:423`, 546 lines), reached through `assetTrack`
  (:400–412) from `resolveSource` (`CompositionBuilder+AudioTracks.swift:61`) and from the
  48 kHz copy (`AudioRateCopy.swift:320–345`).
- Direct callers of `firstTrack(of:mediaType: .audio)`: `Transcriber+Extract.swift:106`,
  `VoiceRenderer.swift:66`, `RampAudioRenderer.swift:116`, `IsolationRenderer.swift:109`,
  `ReverseRenderer.swift:201` (574 lines), `RampAudioCache.swift:136` and `:191`.
  `CompositionBuilder+Silence.swift:49` reads the bundled `Silence.caf` and is unaffected.
- The four cache passes take `loadTracks(withMediaType: .audio)?.first`:
  peaks `MediaImporter.swift:478`, loudness :506, sync features :537, speech :581.
- The 48 kHz copy is keyed by the file alone (`AudioRateCopy.swift:56–70`, "path|size|mtime|v")
  and substituted per media id (`:320–345`), so two streams of one 44.1 kHz file would collide.
- The reversed copy is one movie per media, `cache/reversed/<media>-<digest>.mov`
  (`ReverseCache.swift:64–65`), carrying the first audio track.
- Readers that do NOT need changing: everything that reads the built composition's tracks —
  `ScrubGrains.swift:75`, `ExportMixRead.swift:50`, `ExporterWriter+Audio.swift:42`,
  `ExporterWriter+Settings.swift:69`, `ExporterWriter.swift:141`, `ProcessedLoudness.swift:210`,
  `ExporterLoudness.swift:109`, `ExportWebMWriter.swift:108`.

**Matroska and ffmpeg also take the first audio stream.**
- `core/src/container.rs` (358 lines; new-module cap 400) indexes "its first video track and its
  first audio track" (:1–5, :90–94); `rc_container_sample`'s track argument is `VIDEO = 0`,
  `AUDIO = 1` (:34–37). `ContainerRewrapWriter.swift` (539) copies those two. #216-R records it.
  OBS records Matroska by default.
- The opt-in ffmpeg step maps `-map 0:a:0?` (`FFmpegRewrap+Plan.swift:233`).

**The caches are per media id.**
- `cache/peaks/<id>.bin`, `cache/speech/<id>.bin` (`MediaCacheFiles.swift:101–118`, 452 lines),
  `cache/loudness/<id>.bin` (AU-10), `cache/sync/<id>.bin` and `.pcm` (SY-11),
  `cache/transcripts/<id>.json` (R6-3), `cache/device-transcripts/<id>-<lang>.json`
  (`DeviceTranscriptCache.swift:102`).
- `MediaCacheLoader` memoises by `UInt32` media id (`MediaPeaks.swift:226`); `ClipLoudness`,
  `MediaSpeech`, `DuckSpeech`, `AudioDynamicsLevels`, `SilenceDetector` and `AudioSync`
  (`AudioSync.swift:240–273`, features, samples and speech by media) all read through media ids.
- The loudness cache stores stereo as `zL, zR, zLR` per 10 ms (AU-10), so a left or right
  pick's level is already measurable (AU-35's matrix). A file of more than two channels is read
  again as two. The speech cache is one mono mixdown on Silero's 32 ms grid (silence.md), so a
  stereo file with one person per side has no per-person speech today.
- silence.md: "The probabilities are a per-media CACHE, never computed at feature time." The
  switch obeys it: it reads caches and does arithmetic.

**Channels.** `audio.channels` (AU-34: both, left, right, swapped) is a pick at the head of the
tap. The tap accepts any channel count (`AudioTap.swift:141–170`, 507 lines). What AVFoundation
hands the tap, and what the export's mix does, for a stream of more than two channels has never
been measured (SW-S1).

**Links are pairs.** `Clip.linked` names one partner, mutually (`core/src/edit_link.rs`, 335;
AU-90…AU-97). Picture plus three sound tracks cannot be one linked set today.

**What the switch can build on.**
- Synchronize Audio's shape: `read` takes everything off the document once, `plan` is pure and
  answers ops or every reason it refuses (`AudioSync.swift:1–60`, 551 lines). The switch copies
  that shape.
- A hidden track's clips are not decoded: video is placed only when `instance.shows_video()`
  (`core/src/evaluate.rs:451`; `nest.rs:140`), and sound is placed when `plays_audio()`, which
  reads only `enabled.audio` (`nest.rs:153`). A hidden angle track costs no decode and still
  sounds.
- The plan's A/B assignment puts a timeline track's adjacent clips on one composition track
  (`evaluate.rs:433`); the decoder budget warns past eight video composition tracks
  (`plan.rs:19`). A program track of alternating cameras is therefore one composition track
  whose source changes at each cut (SW-S2 (a)).
- `MAX_CLIPS` is 4,096, nested clips included (`core/src/format.rs:27`, `check_caps` :49).
- No existing op copies a piece of a clip to another track at the same time: `duplicate`
  places a copy one selection-span later; `add_blurred_background` copies a whole clip to a new
  back track. Computing a piece's `in` in Swift would break D2-1 and `source_window.rs`'s "the
  one way a source in point moves". SW1 adds the op.
- `op_table.rs` is 374 lines against its 400 cap; `Kind::Ranges` (a list of `[from, to]`) and
  `Kind::Index` already exist (`op_table.rs:137–161`).
- Nest clips have no in point (`nest.rs:22`): a split nest replays from its top. A multicam clip
  built as a nest would need one; the program track does not.
- `play_preview` (dev tool, G-36) answers the frames a window's preview composed; it is the
  instrument for SW-S2.

**Sizes that set tolls.** `ProjectSnapshot.swift` 1,454 (over; `ClipSource` :901, `ClipSnapshot`
:1029, `TrackSnapshot` :447); `MediaImporter.swift` 589; `AppDelegate+Menus.swift` 554;
`AudioPane.swift` 554; `ReverseRenderer.swift` 574; `Playback.swift` 592; `AudioSync.swift` 551;
`AgentCatalog+Clips.swift` 574; `ContainerRewrapWriter.swift` 539; `core/src/model.rs` 570;
`core/src/edit_clip.rs` 616 (over, known debt; this bet adds nothing to it);
`core/src/container.rs` 358 of 400. `AgentServer.swift`, `EditorViewController.swift` and
`TimelineView.swift` are frozen. `RC_FORMAT_VERSION` is 37 (`format.rs:18`). `ClipSource.media`
is matched in 65 places across 39 files, so a new stream or channel is decoded BESIDE that case,
not into it.

### Decisions to record or amend

Drafts, in the style of `designs/spec/11-decisions/`. Each is recorded in
`designs/spec/11-decisions/creator-jobs.md` before its phase's code.

**Scope (offered to CJ0 for numbering).**
- **CJ-? (SW scope) — Multicam is in, as a program track over angle tracks.** Synced camera
  clips (angles) stay whole on their own tracks; a program track holds the shots, each an
  ordinary clip copied from an angle at the same time. Switch by Speaker writes the program
  track, Switch Angle re-picks a shot, and the Angle Viewer shows every angle and switches while
  playing. There is no multicam source kind and no nest in point: every shot can be rolled,
  trimmed, graded and deleted like any clip, and spec §2's one kind of track holds. Draft text
  for spec §1: "Multicam is in (CJ-?, SW-10, SW-90): synced angles stay whole on their own
  tracks and a program track holds the shots, each an ordinary clip; there is no multicam
  clip."

**SW1 — the piece copy and Switch Angle.**
- **SW-10 — The switch writes a program track; it does not cut the cameras in place.** The
  orchestrator's first reading was picture-only cuts on the stacked camera tracks (`split` every
  camera at every cut, `set_enabled {video: false}` on the pieces not shown). Rejected: it makes
  two to three clips per shot where the program track makes one (a four-camera, three-hour show
  at 8 s shots is about 5,400 against about 1,350 — the stacked form passes `MAX_CLIPS`); moving
  one cut means trimming pieces on two or three tracks, where on the program track it is an
  ordinary roll; and re-picking means splitting a disabled piece first. Both forms decode one
  camera at a time, since hidden and disabled pictures are not placed (`evaluate.rs:451`).
- **SW-11 — `copy_pieces {clip, track, ranges, video?, audio?}`.** Copies the pieces of `clip`
  between each range's ends onto `track` at the same times, with fresh ids. `ranges` is a list
  of `[from, to]` project times; each end is snapped as `split` snaps its `at`; the ranges are
  sorted, must not overlap one another and must lie inside the clip. `video` and `audio`, when
  given, set each piece's `enabled` switches; absent, a piece keeps the clip's. Refused, each in
  its own sentence: a nest clip ("clip N is a nest: a piece of it would replay the nest from its
  first frame"); a range outside the clip; overlapping ranges; a locked destination; a
  destination holding a clip over a range ("track T holds clip C between A and B"). `Err` for
  an unknown clip or track. An empty `ranges` is an identity. A copy has no transition, and its
  `linked` (or, after SW7a, its `link`) is cleared. Allowed inside a nest through `scope`.
- **SW-12 — A piece is exactly the middle a `split` at its two ends would leave.** Its source
  window, a ramp's map and rate (SR-18), its actions clipped to it, a graphic's `in` and
  `length` (G-9) and its words rebased (W-3) all come from `split`'s own arithmetic, called on a
  scratch copy; `copy_pieces` has no source arithmetic of its own. A piece of a synced, drift-
  corrected angle (SY-8's `set_speed`) therefore plays the angle's frames at the angle's times.
- **SW-13 — Clip ▸ Switch Angle ▸ re-picks one shot.** The submenu lists, for the one selected
  clip, every other media clip with pictures in the same container whose span covers the
  selected clip's whole span, front track first, named by clip name else media name, up to
  nine. Choosing one deletes the shot and `copy_pieces` the angle over the same span onto the
  same track with the shot's `enabled` switches, as one undo step "Switch Angle". The tool
  `switch_angle {clip, angle}` does the same and refuses an angle that does not cover the shot.
- **SW-14 — A re-picked shot keeps its span, its switches and its transition, and nothing
  else.** The new piece is the angle's own: a punch-in scale, a grade or an action the old shot
  carried does not carry over, and the guide says so. Its transition is put back with
  `add_transition` at the old kind and duration when the angle's handles allow it, else dropped
  and the step's name says "Switch Angle (transition removed)".

**SW2 — Switch by Speaker.**
- **SW-20 — The inputs.** Angles are the selected clips with pictures (two to nine). Speakers
  are pairs of a microphone and an angle: a microphone is a selected clip that plays sound, and
  its angle is the camera showing that person — any angle, the wide included. The default
  pairing: a microphone that is itself an angle (a lavalier into the camera) pairs with itself;
  the others pair, in track order front to back, with the remaining angles in track order. The
  wide is optional and is the angle no microphone names, when exactly one is left. The range is
  the In/Out range when set, else the span every angle covers. A microphone's steps outside its
  own clip count as silent. The switch trusts the placement; it does not check sync, and the
  guide says to run Synchronize Audio first.
- **SW-21 — A microphone is active when its voice is its own.** On a 10 ms timeline grid over
  the range, for each microphone m: its level ℓ_m(k) is 10·log10 of the loudness cache's
  K-weighted mean square, through the clip's own channel matrix (AU-35) and source map,
  averaged over 100 ms; its voice v_m(k) is the speech cache's probability for the 32 ms chunk
  holding that step's source time. P_m, its own speech level, is the 90th percentile of ℓ_m over
  steps with v_m ≥ 0.5 (a person's own voice is the loudest thing on their microphone); F_m, its
  floor, is the 10th percentile over steps with v_m < 0.5. m is active at k when v_m(k) ≥ 0.5,
  ℓ_m(k) ≥ P_m − `bleed_db` (default 15 dB) and ℓ_m(k) ≥ F_m + 6 dB. When two or more are
  active and one's ℓ − P exceeds every other's by `dominance_db` (default 8 dB), only it is
  active. The four numbers are provisional until SW-S4 sets them.
- **SW-22 — Turns become shots.** One active microphone is that person; two or more is
  crosstalk; none is nobody. A person's turn bridges their gaps under 0.5 s. A turn shorter than
  `min_turn` (1.0 s) starts no shot. Crosstalk lasting `crosstalk_min` (1.0 s) or longer shows
  the wide, or holds the current shot when there is no wide or `crosstalk` is `hold`. Nobody
  holds the current shot. A new shot starts `lead` (0.2 s) before the turn's first active step,
  snapped to the frame grid. A shot shorter than `min_shot` (2.0 s) is merged into the shot
  before it (the first shot into the one after). The range opens on the wide when there is one,
  else on the first speaker. An optional `wide_after` (off by default) cuts to the wide for
  `min_shot` once one person has held the screen that long.
- **SW-23 — What the switch writes, as one undo step "Switch by Speaker".** A new front track
  named "Program"; one `copy_pieces` per angle with that angle's shot ranges and
  `audio: false`; each angle track hidden (`set_track {hidden: true}`) when every clip on it in
  the range is an angle, else each such angle clip's picture switched off; and, when "Mute the
  cameras' own sound" is on, `set_enabled {audio: false}` on every angle that is not also a
  microphone. That box defaults on when no microphone is an angle. Microphones are never edited.
  With `track` (the sheet's "Replace the shots on"), the switch writes onto that track, after a
  `lift_range`-style clear of it alone over the range, instead of adding one.
- **SW-24 — It refuses, naming every reason at once (SY-1's form).** Fewer than two angles; a
  speaker without a microphone; one microphone for two or more speakers ("each person needs
  their own microphone" until SW8); a microphone whose loudness or speech is still being
  analysed; a microphone in which no speech was found; an angle that does not cover the range;
  and a result that would pass `MAX_CLIPS` ("Switch by Speaker would add N clips to M; the most
  is 4,096 — raise the minimum shot").
- **SW-25 — The switch reads caches and computes nothing else.** The loudness and speech caches
  are read through the clip (its source map, channel matrix and, after SW4, its audio source);
  no audio is decoded at feature time (silence.md's rule). The planner is a pure function in
  `SpeakerSwitch.swift`, probe-callable, readings in and shots or refusals out.
- **SW-26 — The sheet and the tool take the same arguments.** `switch_by_speaker {speakers:
  [{mic, angle}], wide?, min_shot?, min_turn?, lead?, crosstalk?: "wide"|"hold", bleed_db?,
  dominance_db?, wide_after?, mute_cameras?, track?, apply?}`. `apply: false` answers the shots
  (`[{start, end, angle}]`) and the ops' count without editing, so an agent can show a plan
  before applying it. Applied, it answers the program track and the shots.
- **SW-27 — The proof's speech is made on the Mac.** Two macOS voices (`say -v`) read a scripted
  turn table; each microphone is its speaker at 0 dB plus the other at a set bleed plus pink
  noise. The table is the ground truth, so every cut is checked to the frame.
- **SW-29 — reserved for the owner's verdict on a real episode (JOB-51).**

**SW3 — every audio track, played.**

- **SW-36 — The Sound tab's Source section.** First in the Sound sub-tab, shown when a selected

**SW4 — every audio track, measured.**

**SW5 — OBS's Matroska.**

**SW7a — link groups.**
- **SW-70 — A link is a group (amends AU-90).** Draft: "Amended by SW-70: `Clip.link` (format

### Spikes

Each runs on Release, its rule fixed here before the run, its record in the road map.

- **SW-S1 — What AVFoundation does with several audio tracks and with many channels.** Runs in
  CJ0. Fixtures: a MOV and an MP4 with video and three AAC tracks of distinct tones; a 6-channel
  48 kHz 24-bit WAV with a distinct tone per channel, once without a channel layout (as
  recorders write) and once with a discrete layout; a 6-channel AAC; the owner's iPhone 18 Pro
  clip with Spatial Audio on; an OBS Hybrid MP4.
  - (a) Order and identity. **Rule:** if `tracks(withMediaType: .audio)` lists the tracks in the
    container's order and track k, inserted in a composition and exported, nulls within −90 dB
    of ffmpeg's `-map 0:a:k` decode after alignment, stream k is AVFoundation's k-th audio track
    (SW-30); otherwise streams are ordered by track ID and that is recorded.
  - (b) The tap's channels. **Rule:** if the tap's `prepare` reports six channels and each
    channel's spectrum peaks at its own tone at least 40 dB above every other, in AVPlayer AND in
    the export's `AVAssetReaderAudioMixOutput`, a channel is picked in the tap (SW-60's tap
    branch); if either fails, a channel source is a mono copy (the copy branch).
  - (c) The default fold. **Rule:** if today's export puts every tone in both sides within 1 dB
    of one another and of every other tone, AVFoundation's fold stands; otherwise Frame Job folds
    (SW-61).
  - (d) Cache reads. **Rule:** if `AVAssetReaderTrackOutput` in float, non-interleaved, with no
    channel-count key, delivers all N channels for the WAV, the 6-channel AAC and the iPhone's
    tracks, the cache passes read a channel directly; otherwise they read the copy.
  - (e) A movie with several audio tracks written. **Rule:** if `AVAssetWriter` writes a `.mov`
    with video and three LPCM tracks that AVFoundation reads back as three tracks in order, the
    reversed copy carries every track (SW-33); otherwise a reversed CAF per stream.
  - (f) Real files. Record only: each track's codec, channels, title and whether it decodes. A
    track that does not decode is not listed (SW-30).
- **SW-S2 — Four 4K angles, a thousand shots, three hours.** Runs in CJ0 on synthetic 4K (and
  again at SW9a on the owner's files). This is the survey's multi-stream 4K and multi-hour
  measurement, scoped to what this bet promises; it is a measurement, not performance work.
  - (a) Cuts on one composition track. Two 4K30 long-GOP angles (H.264 at 100 Mb/s as the GH5
    writes, HEVC Main 10, and ProRes 422 HQ) alternating every 2–8 s for five minutes on the
    program track, at Full quality. **Rule:** at least 99 % of due frames composed
    (`play_preview`) keeps the plan's assignment; below that, SW2 makes the plan put a track's
    adjacent clips of different media on two composition tracks, and re-measures.
  - (b) Rebuild. A two-hour timeline: four hidden 4K angle tracks, two microphones, a 1,000-shot
    program track. **Rule:** an edit's rebuild (from `Playback.update` to the item ready) within
    1.5 s and one `copy_pieces` of 1,000 ranges applied within 0.5 s, or the times are written in
    the guide and a candidate issue is filed in the Performance project; no proxies are built in
    this bet.
  - (c) Angles at once. 1, 2, 3 and 4 4K angles in the quadrants of a 1080p canvas for 60 s at
    Half and Full. **Rule:** the largest N with at least 98 % of frames composed at Half is the
    viewer's live cell count (SW-91): N ≥ 4, four live cells; N of 2–3, live up to N and the rest
    refreshed when paused; N < 2, every cell refreshed only when paused or after a switch.
  - (d) Long files. Seek and play at 0:30, 1:00, 2:00 and 2:59 in a three-hour 4K file. Record
    the time to the first frame.
- **SW-S3 — Mouth activity on a one-microphone show.** Runs before SW8, on the owner's
  S-POD-1MIC. Vision's face landmarks (SW-80) at ten samples a second per 1080p angle;
  ground truth from S-POD-2CAM's two-microphone switch, with only one microphone given.
  **Rule:** at least 85 % agreement on single-speaker speech seconds and at least 4× realtime
  per angle: SW8 is built as SW-81 says. 70–85 %: built with SW-82's hedge. Under 70 %: SW8 is
  not built; a candidate issue records the numbers.
- **SW-S4 — The switch's numbers on real speech.** Runs inside SW2, once its planner exists.
  Fixtures: F-TURNS at bleed −12, −18 and −24 dB and noise floors of −55 and −45 dBFS, and a
  five-minute excerpt of S-POD-2CAM. The real excerpt's truth is the steps where one
  microphone's ℓ − P exceeds the other's by 20 dB (unambiguous steps only). **Rule:** the
  defaults of SW-21 and SW-22 are the values that make every synthetic case place every cut
  within one frame of the table and that maximise agreement on the excerpt. SW2 ships its
  defaults when the excerpt agrees on at least 90 % of unambiguous seconds with no shot of a
  silent listener lasting `min_shot` or more; otherwise SW2 ships with the sheet's bleed row
  shown by default, the guide naming the case and the numbers recorded.

  count does not change while presses are recorded (the dev tool counts rebuilds).
- **Mutants** (2). A press applied at once rather than at stop (W2); a press within a frame kept
  as a second cut (probe).
- **Manual checks.** **JOB-57 — Switching while playing.** Do: play an episode and press 1 and 2
  as the speakers change. Expect: playback never stutters at a press, and the cuts land where
  pressed.
- **Depends on.** SW9a.
- **Questions for the owner at phase time.** (1) Apply at stop (recommended) or edit live?

### Samples and fixtures

**From the owner** (the GH5 and the iPhone 18 Pro; each row goes into `samples/README.md` with
what it measures):
- **S-POD-2CAM** — ten to fifteen minutes of two people talking: the GH5 on one person, the
  iPhone on the other, both 4K, each person on their own microphone (two separate recorder files,
  or two OBS tracks), a clap at the start; turn-taking, short replies, laughter and some talking
  over. A third angle (a wide from a second phone or the Mac's camera through Frame Job's
  recorder) if possible. Measures SW-S4, SW2's JOB-51, SW-S2 on real codecs, SW-S3's ground
  truth.
- **S-POD-SPLIT** — the same kind of conversation on a wireless kit recording both people into
  one camera's stereo track (left and right), if the owner has one. Measures SW6.
- **S-POD-1MIC** — the same conversation with one microphone between the two people and the two
  cameras. Measures SW-S3 and SW8.
- **S-OBS** — an OBS recording of the screen with the mix on track 1, a microphone on track 2
  and the desktop on track 3, once as `.mkv` and once as Hybrid MP4. Measures SW3 and SW5.
- **S-IPHONE-SPATIAL** — a short iPhone 18 Pro clip with Spatial Audio on. Measures SW-S1 (f):
  how many audio tracks the phone writes and whether each decodes.
- **S-RECORDER** — a multitrack file from a recorder or mixer (RØDECaster Pro II, Zoom F-series
  or H-series in multitrack mode, a MixPre), if the owner has one. Measures SW6.

**Synthetic, made by the proofs** (ffmpeg and macOS `say`; no proof waits for a sample):
- **F-TURNS** — two macOS voices reading a scripted turn table (turns, short replies under 1 s,
  stretches of talking over, pauses); each microphone is its voice at 0 dB, the other at a set
  bleed (−12, −18, −24 dB) and pink noise (−55, −45 dBFS); three 1080p colour-card "cameras"
  (one per person and a wide) with burned-in frame counters. The table is the truth (SW-27).
- **F-MULTITRACK** — MOV, MP4 and MKV files with video and three audio tracks (distinct tones,
  and distinct speech placements for SW4), one at 44.1 kHz.
- **F-POLY** — a 6-channel 48 kHz 24-bit WAV, a tone or a voice per channel, with and without a
  channel layout; and a 6-channel AAC.
- **F-SPLIT** — a stereo file with one voice per side and bleed between them.
- **F-4K** — ten-minute 3840×2160 sources at 29.97 and 59.94 fps in H.264 at 100 Mb/s, HEVC
  Main 10 and ProRes 422 HQ, with noise so the encoders work (VideoToolbox encoders through
  ffmpeg), for SW-S2.

### Risks

- **AVFoundation and many channels.** What the tap and the export's mix see for a stream of more
  than two channels is unmeasured; SW-S1 decides between the tap and a copy, and the copy costs
  temporary disk (about 0.5 GB an hour per channel at 24-bit mono) and render time.
- **Cuts between long-GOP 4K files on one composition track may hitch.** SW-S2 (a) measures it;
  the fix is a plan change.
- **Rebuild time with a thousand shots** is unmeasured (SW-S2 (b)); the owner's order puts
  performance work after features, so a shortfall becomes a recorded limit and an issue.
- **Bleed and loud laughter.** One margin will not suit every room; SW-S4 sets the defaults and
  the sheet exposes the margin.
- **Sync.** The switch trusts the placement. A slipped or moved shot falls out of sync with the
  microphones like any synced clip; the guide says so.
- **`MAX_CLIPS`.** A three-hour show at a two-second minimum can pass 4,096; the switch refuses
  first and says what to raise.
- **Hidden angles still sound.** Camera scratch audio doubles the microphones unless muted; the
  switch mutes non-microphone angles by default.
- **Cache volume.** Per-source caches multiply the sync features (23 MB an hour each) and speech
  files; SW-41 makes only the sources clips play.
- **Link groups change a format-28 field and every link rule.** AP9's proof re-runs whole; one
  mutant per rule.
- **Stream order.** If AVFoundation's order differs from the container's (SW-S1 (a)), track names
  in other apps will not match Frame Job's numbers.
- **iPhone Spatial Audio** may add tracks AVFoundation cannot decode on this Mac; they are left
  out (SW-30), and track 1 stays what every build has played.
- **Mouth activity** fails on profiles, small faces in wide shots, beards and hands over mouths;
  SW-S3 gates SW8.
- **Four live 4K decodes** may exceed the Mac's decoders; SW-S2 (c) sets the viewer's live cells.
- **Shared files.** `op_table.rs` (374 of 400), `AppDelegate+Menus.swift` (554) and
  `ProjectSnapshot.swift` (1,454) take rows from every bet; the tolls land in CJ0.

### Not in this bet

Lifted non-goals that this bet does not build, and why, each to be filed as a candidate issue
when the road map closes:
- **A multicam source kind** (one clip holding every angle, as Final Cut Pro's): the program
  track does the same jobs with ordinary clips (SW-10, SW-90).
- **Proxies:** only if SW-S2 shows a shortfall, as a Performance-project issue.
- **Virtual angles from one wide camera** (cropping to each face): bet 3's subject tracking can
  supply the framing; a candidate after VR.
- **Laughter to the wide shot:** needs Find Clips' Sound Analysis cache; a candidate after FC.
- **Telling speakers apart by voice on one microphone with no faces** (diarization): Apple's
  frameworks have no on-device diarization; AssemblyAI's speaker labels would make it a
  key-gated cloud feature. A candidate, keyed if built.
- **Layouts during crosstalk** (side by side): bet 6's layouts can supply them; a candidate.
- **Exporting the multicam edit to another editor** (FCPXML, AAF): a candidate.
- **Live multi-camera capture and remote guests:** the survey's "not worth chasing"; no longer a
  non-goal, but not built here.
- **A multitrack movie as an export:** AU-101 chose separate stem files, and that stands.

## Bet 5 — Switch by Speaker, and read every audio track of a file

### Goal

A creator records a video podcast or an interview with two to four cameras and a microphone per
person. They line the files up with Synchronize Audio, select them, and choose Clip ▸ Switch by
Speaker…. Frame Job cuts to whoever is talking. It judges each microphone's speech against that
microphone's own level, so a guest's voice leaking into the host's microphone does not cut to
the host. It shows the wide shot while two people talk over each other, holds a minimum shot
length, and lets short replies ("yeah", "mm") pass without a cut. The result is one undo step:
a new Program track of ordinary clips, each a piece of one camera, over the cameras kept whole
and hidden on their own tracks. The microphones are not touched. Every cut can be rolled like
any other cut, and Clip ▸ Switch Angle re-picks the camera for one shot. Later phases add a
one-microphone mode that reads mouth movement with Vision, and an Angle Viewer that shows every
camera at once and switches while the timeline plays.

Separately, Frame Job stops reading only the first audio track of a file. An OBS recording with
the mix on track 1, the microphone on track 2 and the desktop on track 3 imports all three. A
recorder or mixer file with many channels in one track (a RØDECaster Pro II, a Zoom F-series,
a MixPre) offers each channel as its own source, and so does a wireless kit that records two
people on the left and right of one stereo track. Each track or channel can be placed as its own
clip with its own audio chain, and Detach Audio makes one linked sound clip per track. Every
measurement — the waveform, loudness, Normalize, Enhance Voice, Duck by Speech, Remove Silences,
Synchronize Audio, transcription — reads the track or channel the clip plays.

Every command has its MCP tool. No phase needs a key.

### Owner's answers applied

- **All six bets are in one road map.** This is bet 5, prefix SW; its phases are SW1–SW9b.
- **Every spec §1 non-goal is lifted.** For this bet that means multicam. The bet builds
  multicam in full: synced angles, a program track of shots, re-picking, an Angle Viewer and
  switching while playing (SW1, SW2, SW9a, SW9b). It does this without a multicam source kind:
  the shots are ordinary clips on an ordinary track (SW-10, SW-90). That is a design choice, not
  a non-goal; the owner can ask for a multicam clip instead at SW9a.
- **§11 decisions that implement a non-goal stand until a phase amends them in writing.** This
  bet amends none of them. Nest clips keep having no in point (`core/src/nest.rs:22`), there is
  still one kind of track (spec §2), and the effect vocabulary stays closed (R5-1).
- **Input Monitoring.** Not used by this bet.
- **The key rule.** Nothing in this bet uses a language model or a cloud model. Switch by
  Speaker reads the loudness cache, Silero VAD's speech cache and, in SW8, Vision face
  landmarks — all on the device, none needing a key. The Assistant can call the bet's tools on
  its own key, as it calls every tool. Transcribing a second audio track with AssemblyAI needs
  the AssemblyAI key exactly as transcribing the first does today.
- **Lead segments.** Video podcasts are the third segment, so the switch (SW1, SW2) is
  scheduled after the first phases of bets 1–4. Reading every audio track (SW3, SW4, SW5) also
  serves the first segment: screen recordists who record with OBS keep their microphone on its
  own track. The orchestrator's default lets those three phases start early, in a lane of their
  own.
- **Real use.** The owner cuts one real video per lead segment alongside bet 1. For podcasts,
  JOB-51 asks the owner to cut one real episode with Switch by Speaker once SW2 lands; the
  verdict is recorded as SW-29, the way GR-9 recorded grading's trial.
- **Build arrangement.** Every format number below is provisional ("format 38p") until its
  phase lands; the integrator renumbers on collision. Decision IDs are SW-n0…SW-n9 per phase;
  scope-level drafts are offered to CJ0 for numbering.

### How it fits the tree

At `d0661e5d`. Line counts are `wc -l`.

**A media is one file with one sound.**
- `Media` (`core/src/model.rs:162–192`, the file 570 lines) records `has_audio: bool` and
  nothing about how many audio tracks or channels the file has. Its `speech` spans
  (format 29, AU-110) belong to the file as a whole.
- `add_media` treats a path already in the list as an identity (`core/src/edit_track.rs:476`,
  the doc above it: "two entries for one path would each carry their own bookmark, thumbnails
  and peaks"). A second audio track therefore cannot be a second media row; it must be
  something a CLIP chooses.
- `Source::Media` is `{media, in, reversed}` (`core/src/model.rs:292–315`). `reversed` is the
  precedent for a fact about what a clip reads that changes neither the plan's structure nor
  the recipe.

**Every reader takes the first audio track.**
- The probe counts audio tracks and keeps only whether there is one
  (`app/Sources/MediaImporter.swift:79`, `hasAudio: !audioTracks.isEmpty` at :114).
- The builder's one synchronous track lookup answers `.first`
  (`app/Sources/CompositionBuilder.swift:423`, 546 lines), reached through `assetTrack`
  (:400–412) from `resolveSource` (`CompositionBuilder+AudioTracks.swift:61`) and from the
  48 kHz copy (`AudioRateCopy.swift:320–345`).
- Direct callers of `firstTrack(of:mediaType: .audio)`: `Transcriber+Extract.swift:106`,
  `VoiceRenderer.swift:66`, `RampAudioRenderer.swift:116`, `IsolationRenderer.swift:109`,
  `ReverseRenderer.swift:201` (574 lines), `RampAudioCache.swift:136` and `:191`.
  `CompositionBuilder+Silence.swift:49` reads the bundled `Silence.caf` and is unaffected.
- The four cache passes take `loadTracks(withMediaType: .audio)?.first`:
  peaks `MediaImporter.swift:478`, loudness :506, sync features :537, speech :581.
- The 48 kHz copy is keyed by the file alone (`AudioRateCopy.swift:56–70`, "path|size|mtime|v")
  and substituted per media id (`:320–345`), so two streams of one 44.1 kHz file would collide.
- The reversed copy is one movie per media, `cache/reversed/<media>-<digest>.mov`
  (`ReverseCache.swift:64–65`), carrying the first audio track.
- Readers that do NOT need changing: everything that reads the built composition's tracks —
  `ScrubGrains.swift:75`, `ExportMixRead.swift:50`, `ExporterWriter+Audio.swift:42`,
  `ExporterWriter+Settings.swift:69`, `ExporterWriter.swift:141`, `ProcessedLoudness.swift:210`,
  `ExporterLoudness.swift:109`, `ExportWebMWriter.swift:108`.

**Matroska and ffmpeg also take the first audio stream.**
- `core/src/container.rs` (358 lines; new-module cap 400) indexes "its first video track and its
  first audio track" (:1–5, :90–94); `rc_container_sample`'s track argument is `VIDEO = 0`,
  `AUDIO = 1` (:34–37). `ContainerRewrapWriter.swift` (539) copies those two. #216-R records it.
  OBS records Matroska by default.
- The opt-in ffmpeg step maps `-map 0:a:0?` (`FFmpegRewrap+Plan.swift:233`).

**The caches are per media id.**
- `cache/peaks/<id>.bin`, `cache/speech/<id>.bin` (`MediaCacheFiles.swift:101–118`, 452 lines),
  `cache/loudness/<id>.bin` (AU-10), `cache/sync/<id>.bin` and `.pcm` (SY-11),
  `cache/transcripts/<id>.json` (R6-3), `cache/device-transcripts/<id>-<lang>.json`
  (`DeviceTranscriptCache.swift:102`).
- `MediaCacheLoader` memoises by `UInt32` media id (`MediaPeaks.swift:226`); `ClipLoudness`,
  `MediaSpeech`, `DuckSpeech`, `AudioDynamicsLevels`, `SilenceDetector` and `AudioSync`
  (`AudioSync.swift:240–273`, features, samples and speech by media) all read through media ids.
- The loudness cache stores stereo as `zL, zR, zLR` per 10 ms (AU-10), so a left or right
  pick's level is already measurable (AU-35's matrix). A file of more than two channels is read
  again as two. The speech cache is one mono mixdown on Silero's 32 ms grid (silence.md), so a
  stereo file with one person per side has no per-person speech today.
- silence.md: "The probabilities are a per-media CACHE, never computed at feature time." The
  switch obeys it: it reads caches and does arithmetic.

**Channels.** `audio.channels` (AU-34: both, left, right, swapped) is a pick at the head of the
tap. The tap accepts any channel count (`AudioTap.swift:141–170`, 507 lines). What AVFoundation
hands the tap, and what the export's mix does, for a stream of more than two channels has never
been measured (SW-S1).

**Links are pairs.** `Clip.linked` names one partner, mutually (`core/src/edit_link.rs`, 335;
AU-90…AU-97). Picture plus three sound tracks cannot be one linked set today.

**What the switch can build on.**
- Synchronize Audio's shape: `read` takes everything off the document once, `plan` is pure and
  answers ops or every reason it refuses (`AudioSync.swift:1–60`, 551 lines). The switch copies
  that shape.
- A hidden track's clips are not decoded: video is placed only when `instance.shows_video()`
  (`core/src/evaluate.rs:451`; `nest.rs:140`), and sound is placed when `plays_audio()`, which
  reads only `enabled.audio` (`nest.rs:153`). A hidden angle track costs no decode and still
  sounds.
- The plan's A/B assignment puts a timeline track's adjacent clips on one composition track
  (`evaluate.rs:433`); the decoder budget warns past eight video composition tracks
  (`plan.rs:19`). A program track of alternating cameras is therefore one composition track
  whose source changes at each cut (SW-S2 (a)).
- `MAX_CLIPS` is 4,096, nested clips included (`core/src/format.rs:27`, `check_caps` :49).
- No existing op copies a piece of a clip to another track at the same time: `duplicate`
  places a copy one selection-span later; `add_blurred_background` copies a whole clip to a new
  back track. Computing a piece's `in` in Swift would break D2-1 and `source_window.rs`'s "the
  one way a source in point moves". SW1 adds the op.
- `op_table.rs` is 374 lines against its 400 cap; `Kind::Ranges` (a list of `[from, to]`) and
  `Kind::Index` already exist (`op_table.rs:137–161`).
- Nest clips have no in point (`nest.rs:22`): a split nest replays from its top. A multicam clip
  built as a nest would need one; the program track does not.
- `play_preview` (dev tool, G-36) answers the frames a window's preview composed; it is the
  instrument for SW-S2.

**Sizes that set tolls.** `ProjectSnapshot.swift` 1,454 (over; `ClipSource` :901, `ClipSnapshot`
:1029, `TrackSnapshot` :447); `MediaImporter.swift` 589; `AppDelegate+Menus.swift` 554;
`AudioPane.swift` 554; `ReverseRenderer.swift` 574; `Playback.swift` 592; `AudioSync.swift` 551;
`AgentCatalog+Clips.swift` 574; `ContainerRewrapWriter.swift` 539; `core/src/model.rs` 570;
`core/src/edit_clip.rs` 616 (over, known debt; this bet adds nothing to it);
`core/src/container.rs` 358 of 400. `AgentServer.swift`, `EditorViewController.swift` and
`TimelineView.swift` are frozen. `RC_FORMAT_VERSION` is 37 (`format.rs:18`). `ClipSource.media`
is matched in 65 places across 39 files, so a new stream or channel is decoded BESIDE that case,
not into it.

### Decisions to record or amend

Drafts, in the style of `designs/spec/11-decisions/`. Each is recorded in
`designs/spec/11-decisions/creator-jobs.md` before its phase's code.

**Scope (offered to CJ0 for numbering).**
- **CJ-? (SW scope) — Multicam is in, as a program track over angle tracks.** Synced camera
  clips (angles) stay whole on their own tracks; a program track holds the shots, each an
  ordinary clip copied from an angle at the same time. Switch by Speaker writes the program
  track, Switch Angle re-picks a shot, and the Angle Viewer shows every angle and switches while
  playing. There is no multicam source kind and no nest in point: every shot can be rolled,
  trimmed, graded and deleted like any clip, and spec §2's one kind of track holds. Draft text
  for spec §1: "Multicam is in (CJ-?, SW-10, SW-90): synced angles stay whole on their own
  tracks and a program track holds the shots, each an ordinary clip; there is no multicam
  clip."

**SW1 — the piece copy and Switch Angle.**
- **SW-10 — The switch writes a program track; it does not cut the cameras in place.** The
  orchestrator's first reading was picture-only cuts on the stacked camera tracks (`split` every
  camera at every cut, `set_enabled {video: false}` on the pieces not shown). Rejected: it makes
  two to three clips per shot where the program track makes one (a four-camera, three-hour show
  at 8 s shots is about 5,400 against about 1,350 — the stacked form passes `MAX_CLIPS`); moving
  one cut means trimming pieces on two or three tracks, where on the program track it is an
  ordinary roll; and re-picking means splitting a disabled piece first. Both forms decode one
  camera at a time, since hidden and disabled pictures are not placed (`evaluate.rs:451`).
- **SW-11 — `copy_pieces {clip, track, ranges, video?, audio?}`.** Copies the pieces of `clip`
  between each range's ends onto `track` at the same times, with fresh ids. `ranges` is a list
  of `[from, to]` project times; each end is snapped as `split` snaps its `at`; the ranges are
  sorted, must not overlap one another and must lie inside the clip. `video` and `audio`, when
  given, set each piece's `enabled` switches; absent, a piece keeps the clip's. Refused, each in
  its own sentence: a nest clip ("clip N is a nest: a piece of it would replay the nest from its
  first frame"); a range outside the clip; overlapping ranges; a locked destination; a
  destination holding a clip over a range ("track T holds clip C between A and B"). `Err` for
  an unknown clip or track. An empty `ranges` is an identity. A copy has no transition, and its
  `linked` (or, after SW7a, its `link`) is cleared. Allowed inside a nest through `scope`.
- **SW-12 — A piece is exactly the middle a `split` at its two ends would leave.** Its source
  window, a ramp's map and rate (SR-18), its actions clipped to it, a graphic's `in` and
  `length` (G-9) and its words rebased (W-3) all come from `split`'s own arithmetic, called on a
  scratch copy; `copy_pieces` has no source arithmetic of its own. A piece of a synced, drift-
  corrected angle (SY-8's `set_speed`) therefore plays the angle's frames at the angle's times.
- **SW-13 — Clip ▸ Switch Angle ▸ re-picks one shot.** The submenu lists, for the one selected
  clip, every other media clip with pictures in the same container whose span covers the
  selected clip's whole span, front track first, named by clip name else media name, up to
  nine. Choosing one deletes the shot and `copy_pieces` the angle over the same span onto the
  same track with the shot's `enabled` switches, as one undo step "Switch Angle". The tool
  `switch_angle {clip, angle}` does the same and refuses an angle that does not cover the shot.
- **SW-14 — A re-picked shot keeps its span, its switches and its transition, and nothing
  else.** The new piece is the angle's own: a punch-in scale, a grade or an action the old shot
  carried does not carry over, and the guide says so. Its transition is put back with
  `add_transition` at the old kind and duration when the angle's handles allow it, else dropped
  and the step's name says "Switch Angle (transition removed)".

**SW2 — Switch by Speaker.**
- **SW-20 — The inputs.** Angles are the selected clips with pictures (two to nine). Speakers
  are pairs of a microphone and an angle: a microphone is a selected clip that plays sound, and
  its angle is the camera showing that person — any angle, the wide included. The default
  pairing: a microphone that is itself an angle (a lavalier into the camera) pairs with itself;
  the others pair, in track order front to back, with the remaining angles in track order. The
  wide is optional and is the angle no microphone names, when exactly one is left. The range is
  the In/Out range when set, else the span every angle covers. A microphone's steps outside its
  own clip count as silent. The switch trusts the placement; it does not check sync, and the
  guide says to run Synchronize Audio first.
- **SW-21 — A microphone is active when its voice is its own.** On a 10 ms timeline grid over
  the range, for each microphone m: its level ℓ_m(k) is 10·log10 of the loudness cache's
  K-weighted mean square, through the clip's own channel matrix (AU-35) and source map,
  averaged over 100 ms; its voice v_m(k) is the speech cache's probability for the 32 ms chunk
  holding that step's source time. P_m, its own speech level, is the 90th percentile of ℓ_m over
  steps with v_m ≥ 0.5 (a person's own voice is the loudest thing on their microphone); F_m, its
  floor, is the 10th percentile over steps with v_m < 0.5. m is active at k when v_m(k) ≥ 0.5,
  ℓ_m(k) ≥ P_m − `bleed_db` (default 15 dB) and ℓ_m(k) ≥ F_m + 6 dB. When two or more are
  active and one's ℓ − P exceeds every other's by `dominance_db` (default 8 dB), only it is
  active. The four numbers are provisional until SW-S4 sets them.
- **SW-22 — Turns become shots.** One active microphone is that person; two or more is
  crosstalk; none is nobody. A person's turn bridges their gaps under 0.5 s. A turn shorter than
  `min_turn` (1.0 s) starts no shot. Crosstalk lasting `crosstalk_min` (1.0 s) or longer shows
  the wide, or holds the current shot when there is no wide or `crosstalk` is `hold`. Nobody
  holds the current shot. A new shot starts `lead` (0.2 s) before the turn's first active step,
  snapped to the frame grid. A shot shorter than `min_shot` (2.0 s) is merged into the shot
  before it (the first shot into the one after). The range opens on the wide when there is one,
  else on the first speaker. An optional `wide_after` (off by default) cuts to the wide for
  `min_shot` once one person has held the screen that long.
- **SW-23 — What the switch writes, as one undo step "Switch by Speaker".** A new front track
  named "Program"; one `copy_pieces` per angle with that angle's shot ranges and
  `audio: false`; each angle track hidden (`set_track {hidden: true}`) when every clip on it in
  the range is an angle, else each such angle clip's picture switched off; and, when "Mute the
  cameras' own sound" is on, `set_enabled {audio: false}` on every angle that is not also a
  microphone. That box defaults on when no microphone is an angle. Microphones are never edited.
  With `track` (the sheet's "Replace the shots on"), the switch writes onto that track, after a
  `lift_range`-style clear of it alone over the range, instead of adding one.
- **SW-24 — It refuses, naming every reason at once (SY-1's form).** Fewer than two angles; a
  speaker without a microphone; one microphone for two or more speakers ("each person needs
  their own microphone" until SW8); a microphone whose loudness or speech is still being
  analysed; a microphone in which no speech was found; an angle that does not cover the range;
  and a result that would pass `MAX_CLIPS` ("Switch by Speaker would add N clips to M; the most
  is 4,096 — raise the minimum shot").
- **SW-25 — The switch reads caches and computes nothing else.** The loudness and speech caches
  are read through the clip (its source map, channel matrix and, after SW4, its audio source);
  no audio is decoded at feature time (silence.md's rule). The planner is a pure function in
  `SpeakerSwitch.swift`, probe-callable, readings in and shots or refusals out.
- **SW-26 — The sheet and the tool take the same arguments.** `switch_by_speaker {speakers:
  [{mic, angle}], wide?, min_shot?, min_turn?, lead?, crosstalk?: "wide"|"hold", bleed_db?,
  dominance_db?, wide_after?, mute_cameras?, track?, apply?}`. `apply: false` answers the shots
  (`[{start, end, angle}]`) and the ops' count without editing, so an agent can show a plan
  before applying it. Applied, it answers the program track and the shots.
- **SW-27 — The proof's speech is made on the Mac.** Two macOS voices (`say -v`) read a scripted
  turn table; each microphone is its speaker at 0 dB plus the other at a set bleed plus pink
  noise. The table is the ground truth, so every cut is checked to the frame.
- **SW-29 — reserved for the owner's verdict on a real episode (JOB-51).**

**SW3 — every audio track, played.**
- **SW-30 — `media.audio_streams` (format 38p).** One entry per audio track, in AVFoundation's
  order (SW-S1 (a)), each `{channels, name?}` — `name` from the track's title metadata (OBS's
  track names, Matroska's TrackEntry Name). Written only when the file has more than one audio
  track or a track of more than two channels, so every other media writes what it did. Stream 0
  is the track every build has read until now. A track that does not decode (SW-S1 (f)) is not

### Spikes

Each runs on Release, its rule fixed here before the run, its record in the road map.

- **SW-S1 — What AVFoundation does with several audio tracks and with many channels.** Runs in
  CJ0. Fixtures: a MOV and an MP4 with video and three AAC tracks of distinct tones; a 6-channel
  48 kHz 24-bit WAV with a distinct tone per channel, once without a channel layout (as
  recorders write) and once with a discrete layout; a 6-channel AAC; the owner's iPhone 18 Pro
  clip with Spatial Audio on; an OBS Hybrid MP4.
  - (a) Order and identity. **Rule:** if `tracks(withMediaType: .audio)` lists the tracks in the
    container's order and track k, inserted in a composition and exported, nulls within −90 dB
    of ffmpeg's `-map 0:a:k` decode after alignment, stream k is AVFoundation's k-th audio track
    (SW-30); otherwise streams are ordered by track ID and that is recorded.
  - (b) The tap's channels. **Rule:** if the tap's `prepare` reports six channels and each
    channel's spectrum peaks at its own tone at least 40 dB above every other, in AVPlayer AND in
    the export's `AVAssetReaderAudioMixOutput`, a channel is picked in the tap (SW-60's tap
    branch); if either fails, a channel source is a mono copy (the copy branch).
  - (c) The default fold. **Rule:** if today's export puts every tone in both sides within 1 dB
    of one another and of every other tone, AVFoundation's fold stands; otherwise Frame Job folds
    (SW-61).
  - (d) Cache reads. **Rule:** if `AVAssetReaderTrackOutput` in float, non-interleaved, with no
    channel-count key, delivers all N channels for the WAV, the 6-channel AAC and the iPhone's
    tracks, the cache passes read a channel directly; otherwise they read the copy.
  - (e) A movie with several audio tracks written. **Rule:** if `AVAssetWriter` writes a `.mov`
    with video and three LPCM tracks that AVFoundation reads back as three tracks in order, the
    reversed copy carries every track (SW-33); otherwise a reversed CAF per stream.
  - (f) Real files. Record only: each track's codec, channels, title and whether it decodes. A
    track that does not decode is not listed (SW-30).
- **SW-S2 — Four 4K angles, a thousand shots, three hours.** Runs in CJ0 on synthetic 4K (and
  again at SW9a on the owner's files). This is the survey's multi-stream 4K and multi-hour
  measurement, scoped to what this bet promises; it is a measurement, not performance work.
  - (a) Cuts on one composition track. Two 4K30 long-GOP angles (H.264 at 100 Mb/s as the GH5
    writes, HEVC Main 10, and ProRes 422 HQ) alternating every 2–8 s for five minutes on the
    program track, at Full quality. **Rule:** at least 99 % of due frames composed
    (`play_preview`) keeps the plan's assignment; below that, SW2 makes the plan put a track's
    adjacent clips of different media on two composition tracks, and re-measures.
  - (b) Rebuild. A two-hour timeline: four hidden 4K angle tracks, two microphones, a 1,000-shot
    program track. **Rule:** an edit's rebuild (from `Playback.update` to the item ready) within
    1.5 s and one `copy_pieces` of 1,000 ranges applied within 0.5 s, or the times are written in
    the guide and a candidate issue is filed in the Performance project; no proxies are built in
    this bet.
  - (c) Angles at once. 1, 2, 3 and 4 4K angles in the quadrants of a 1080p canvas for 60 s at
    Half and Full. **Rule:** the largest N with at least 98 % of frames composed at Half is the
    viewer's live cell count (SW-91): N ≥ 4, four live cells; N of 2–3, live up to N and the rest
    refreshed when paused; N < 2, every cell refreshed only when paused or after a switch.
  - (d) Long files. Seek and play at 0:30, 1:00, 2:00 and 2:59 in a three-hour 4K file. Record
    the time to the first frame.
- **SW-S3 — Mouth activity on a one-microphone show.** Runs before SW8, on the owner's
  S-POD-1MIC. Vision's face landmarks (SW-80) at ten samples a second per 1080p angle;
  ground truth from S-POD-2CAM's two-microphone switch, with only one microphone given.
  **Rule:** at least 85 % agreement on single-speaker speech seconds and at least 4× realtime
  per angle: SW8 is built as SW-81 says. 70–85 %: built with SW-82's hedge. Under 70 %: SW8 is
  not built; a candidate issue records the numbers.
- **SW-S4 — The switch's numbers on real speech.** Runs inside SW2, once its planner exists.
  Fixtures: F-TURNS at bleed −12, −18 and −24 dB and noise floors of −55 and −45 dBFS, and a
  five-minute excerpt of S-POD-2CAM. The real excerpt's truth is the steps where one
  microphone's ℓ − P exceeds the other's by 20 dB (unambiguous steps only). **Rule:** the
  defaults of SW-21 and SW-22 are the values that make every synthetic case place every cut
  within one frame of the table and that maximise agreement on the excerpt. SW2 ships its
  defaults when the excerpt agrees on at least 90 % of unambiguous seconds with no shot of a
  silent listener lasting `min_shot` or more; otherwise SW2 ships with the sheet's bleed row
  shown by default, the guide naming the case and the numbers recorded.

**From the owner** (the GH5 and the iPhone 18 Pro; each row goes into `samples/README.md` with
what it measures):
- **S-POD-2CAM** — ten to fifteen minutes of two people talking: the GH5 on one person, the
  iPhone on the other, both 4K, each person on their own microphone (two separate recorder files,
  or two OBS tracks), a clap at the start; turn-taking, short replies, laughter and some talking
  over. A third angle (a wide from a second phone or the Mac's camera through Frame Job's
  recorder) if possible. Measures SW-S4, SW2's JOB-51, SW-S2 on real codecs, SW-S3's ground
  truth.
- **S-POD-SPLIT** — the same kind of conversation on a wireless kit recording both people into
  one camera's stereo track (left and right), if the owner has one. Measures SW6.
- **S-POD-1MIC** — the same conversation with one microphone between the two people and the two
  cameras. Measures SW-S3 and SW8.
- **S-OBS** — an OBS recording of the screen with the mix on track 1, a microphone on track 2
  and the desktop on track 3, once as `.mkv` and once as Hybrid MP4. Measures SW3 and SW5.
- **S-IPHONE-SPATIAL** — a short iPhone 18 Pro clip with Spatial Audio on. Measures SW-S1 (f):
  how many audio tracks the phone writes and whether each decodes.
- **S-RECORDER** — a multitrack file from a recorder or mixer (RØDECaster Pro II, Zoom F-series
  or H-series in multitrack mode, a MixPre), if the owner has one. Measures SW6.

**Synthetic, made by the proofs** (ffmpeg and macOS `say`; no proof waits for a sample):
- **F-TURNS** — two macOS voices reading a scripted turn table (turns, short replies under 1 s,
  stretches of talking over, pauses); each microphone is its voice at 0 dB, the other at a set
  bleed (−12, −18, −24 dB) and pink noise (−55, −45 dBFS); three 1080p colour-card "cameras"
  (one per person and a wide) with burned-in frame counters. The table is the truth (SW-27).
- **F-MULTITRACK** — MOV, MP4 and MKV files with video and three audio tracks (distinct tones,
  and distinct speech placements for SW4), one at 44.1 kHz.
- **F-POLY** — a 6-channel 48 kHz 24-bit WAV, a tone or a voice per channel, with and without a
  channel layout; and a 6-channel AAC.
- **F-SPLIT** — a stereo file with one voice per side and bleed between them.
- **F-4K** — ten-minute 3840×2160 sources at 29.97 and 59.94 fps in H.264 at 100 Mb/s, HEVC
  Main 10 and ProRes 422 HQ, with noise so the encoders work (VideoToolbox encoders through
  ffmpeg), for SW-S2.

### Risks

- **AVFoundation and many channels.** What the tap and the export's mix see for a stream of more
  than two channels is unmeasured; SW-S1 decides between the tap and a copy, and the copy costs
  temporary disk (about 0.5 GB an hour per channel at 24-bit mono) and render time.
- **Cuts between long-GOP 4K files on one composition track may hitch.** SW-S2 (a) measures it;
  the fix is a plan change.
- **Rebuild time with a thousand shots** is unmeasured (SW-S2 (b)); the owner's order puts
  performance work after features, so a shortfall becomes a recorded limit and an issue.
- **Bleed and loud laughter.** One margin will not suit every room; SW-S4 sets the defaults and
  the sheet exposes the margin.
- **Sync.** The switch trusts the placement. A slipped or moved shot falls out of sync with the
  microphones like any synced clip; the guide says so.
- **`MAX_CLIPS`.** A three-hour show at a two-second minimum can pass 4,096; the switch refuses
  first and says what to raise.
- **Hidden angles still sound.** Camera scratch audio doubles the microphones unless muted; the
  switch mutes non-microphone angles by default.
- **Cache volume.** Per-source caches multiply the sync features (23 MB an hour each) and speech
  files; SW-41 makes only the sources clips play.
- **Link groups change a format-28 field and every link rule.** AP9's proof re-runs whole; one
  mutant per rule.
- **Stream order.** If AVFoundation's order differs from the container's (SW-S1 (a)), track names
  in other apps will not match Frame Job's numbers.
- **iPhone Spatial Audio** may add tracks AVFoundation cannot decode on this Mac; they are left
  out (SW-30), and track 1 stays what every build has played.
- **Mouth activity** fails on profiles, small faces in wide shots, beards and hands over mouths;
  SW-S3 gates SW8.
- **Four live 4K decodes** may exceed the Mac's decoders; SW-S2 (c) sets the viewer's live cells.
- **Shared files.** `op_table.rs` (374 of 400), `AppDelegate+Menus.swift` (554) and
  `ProjectSnapshot.swift` (1,454) take rows from every bet; the tolls land in CJ0.

### Not in this bet

Lifted non-goals that this bet does not build, and why, each to be filed as a candidate issue
when the road map closes:
- **A multicam source kind** (one clip holding every angle, as Final Cut Pro's): the program
  track does the same jobs with ordinary clips (SW-10, SW-90).
- **Proxies:** only if SW-S2 shows a shortfall, as a Performance-project issue.
- **Virtual angles from one wide camera** (cropping to each face): bet 3's subject tracking can
  supply the framing; a candidate after VR.
- **Laughter to the wide shot:** needs Find Clips' Sound Analysis cache; a candidate after FC.
- **Telling speakers apart by voice on one microphone with no faces** (diarization): Apple's
  frameworks have no on-device diarization; AssemblyAI's speaker labels would make it a
  key-gated cloud feature. A candidate, keyed if built.
- **Layouts during crosstalk** (side by side): bet 6's layouts can supply them; a candidate.
- **Exporting the multicam edit to another editor** (FCPXML, AAF): a candidate.
- **Live multi-camera capture and remote guests:** the survey's "not worth chasing"; no longer a
  non-goal, but not built here.
- **A multitrack movie as an export:** AU-101 chose separate stem files, and that stands.

spikes.question: What AVFoundation does with several audio tracks and many channels: (a) does tracks(withMediaType:.audio) follow container order and does track k export exactly; (b) does the MTAudioProcessingTap see every channel of a 6-channel stream unmixed in AVPlayer and in the export's mix reader; (c) what fold does today's export apply to a 6-channel stream; (d) does AVAssetReaderTrackOutput deliver all N channels; (e) can AVAssetWriter write a .mov with several LPCM tracks read back in order; (f) what tracks do the owner's iPhone 18 Pro (Spatial Audio) and OBS Hybrid MP4 files hold, and do they decode. Runs in CJ0.
spikes.rule: (a) container order AND each track nulls within −90 dB of ffmpeg -map 0:a:k → stream k is AVFoundation's k-th audio track, else order by track ID. (b) 6 channels reported and each channel's tone ≥ 40 dB above the others in BOTH player and export → channel pick in the tap, else a mono copy per (file, stream, channel). (c) every tone in both sides within 1 dB of each other → AVFoundation's fold stands, else Frame Job folds at 1/√N. (d) all channels delivered → caches read a channel directly, else from the copy. (e) three tracks read back in order → the reversed copy carries every track, else a reversed CAF per stream. (f) record only; an undecodable track is not listed.

spikes.question: Can this Mac play the switch's output and the Angle Viewer at 4K: (a) cuts between alternating long-GOP 4K sources (H.264 100 Mb/s, HEVC Main 10, ProRes 422 HQ) on one composition track; (b) rebuild time for a 2-hour timeline with four hidden 4K angles, two mics and a 1,000-shot program track, and one copy_pieces of 1,000 ranges; (c) 1–4 4K angles composed at once; (d) seek-and-play in a 3-hour 4K file. Runs in CJ0 on synthetic 4K, again at SW9a on the owner's files.
spikes.rule: (a) ≥ 99 % of due frames composed (play_preview, Full) keeps the plan's assignment; below, SW2 alternates a track's adjacent clips of different media over two composition tracks and re-measures. (b) rebuild ≤ 1.5 s and the apply ≤ 0.5 s, else the times go in the guide and a Performance-project candidate is filed (no proxies built). (c) the largest N with ≥ 98 % composed at Half is the viewer's live cell count: N ≥ 4 four live cells; 2–3 live up to N, rest refreshed on pause; < 2 every cell refreshed only when paused or after a switch. (d) record only.

spikes.question: Does mouth movement from Vision face landmarks (VNDetectFaceLandmarksRequest rev 3, 76-point inner lips, 10 samples/s per 1080p angle) tell who is talking on a one-mic, two-camera conversation, and how fast? Runs before SW8 on S-POD-1MIC, truth from S-POD-2CAM's two-mic switch.
spikes.rule: ≥ 85 % agreement on single-speaker speech seconds and ≥ 4× realtime per angle → SW8 built as SW-81; 70–85 % → built with SW-82's hedge and a 3 s minimum shot; < 70 % → SW8 not built, a candidate issue records the numbers.

spikes.question: What bleed margin, dominance, minimum turn and lead make the switch right on real speech? Runs inside SW2 on F-TURNS (bleed −12/−18/−24 dB, floors −55/−45 dBFS) and a 5-minute excerpt of S-POD-2CAM, truth on unambiguous steps (one mic's ℓ − P exceeds the other's by 20 dB).
spikes.rule: Defaults are the values that place every synthetic cut within one frame and maximise agreement on the excerpt. SW2 ships them when the excerpt agrees on ≥ 90 % of unambiguous seconds with no silent-listener shot of min_shot or longer; otherwise SW2 ships with the sheet's bleed row shown by default, the guide naming the case and the numbers recorded.

shared_needs: A video-analysis lane and per-media Vision cache separate from MediaCacheLane's width-2 audio lane (faces with tracking ids and inner-lip landmarks at 10 samples/s): SW8 needs the lips, VR the face/person rectangles, CO the person masks — one CJ infrastructure phase

AudioSourceKey (media, stream, channel) from SW4: every bet reading per-media audio caches (TX transcripts, FC loudness and laughter, CO hide-camera-while-silent reading the mic's speech) should read through it once SW4 lands

risks: AVFoundation's handling of streams of more than two channels (tap channel count, export fold) is unmeasured; SW-S1 picks tap or copy, and the copy costs temp disk (~0.5 GB/hour per channel) and render time
Alternating long-GOP 4K sources on one composition track may hitch at every cut; SW-S2 (a) measures, the fix is a plan change
Rebuild time with ~1,000 program shots is unmeasured; under features-before-performance a shortfall becomes a recorded limit and a Performance issue, not proxies
Bleed and loud laughter: one margin will not suit every room; SW-S4 sets defaults and the sheet exposes the margin
The switch trusts placement: a slipped or moved shot falls out of sync with the mics like any synced clip
MAX_CLIPS 4,096: a three-hour show at a 2 s minimum can pass it; the switch refuses first, naming what to raise
Hidden angle tracks still sound (plays_audio reads only enabled.audio); camera scratch audio doubles the mics unless muted — the switch mutes non-mic angles by default

Link groups replace format 28's linked and every AP9 rule; AP9's proof re-runs whole, one mutant per rule
If AVFoundation's track order differs from the container's, track numbers will not match other apps' (SW-S1 (a))
iPhone 18 Pro Spatial Audio may add tracks that do not decode; they are left out and track 1 stays what every build played
Vision mouth activity fails on profiles, small faces in wide shots, beards and hands; SW-S3 gates SW8

phases.title: Switching while playing

spikes.question: What AVFoundation does with several audio tracks and many channels: (a) does tracks(withMediaType:.audio) follow container order and does track k export exactly; (b) does the MTAudioProcessingTap see every channel of a 6-channel stream unmixed in AVPlayer and in the export's mix reader; (c) what fold does today's export apply to a 6-channel stream; (d) does AVAssetReaderTrackOutput deliver all N channels; (e) can AVAssetWriter write a .mov with several LPCM tracks read back in order; (f) what tracks do the owner's iPhone 18 Pro (Spatial Audio) and OBS Hybrid MP4 files hold, and do they decode. Runs in CJ0.
spikes.rule: (a) container order AND each track nulls within −90 dB of ffmpeg -map 0:a:k → stream k is AVFoundation's k-th audio track, else order by track ID. (b) 6 channels reported and each channel's tone ≥ 40 dB above the others in BOTH player and export → channel pick in the tap, else a mono copy per (file, stream, channel). (c) every tone in both sides within 1 dB of each other → AVFoundation's fold stands, else Frame Job folds at 1/√N. (d) all channels delivered → caches read a channel directly, else from the copy. (e) three tracks read back in order → the reversed copy carries every track, else a reversed CAF per stream. (f) record only; an undecodable track is not listed.

spikes.question: Can this Mac play the switch's output and the Angle Viewer at 4K: (a) cuts between alternating long-GOP 4K sources (H.264 100 Mb/s, HEVC Main 10, ProRes 422 HQ) on one composition track; (b) rebuild time for a 2-hour timeline with four hidden 4K angles, two mics and a 1,000-shot program track, and one copy_pieces of 1,000 ranges; (c) 1–4 4K angles composed at once; (d) seek-and-play in a 3-hour 4K file. Runs in CJ0 on synthetic 4K, again at SW9a on the owner's files.
spikes.rule: (a) ≥ 99 % of due frames composed (play_preview, Full) keeps the plan's assignment; below, SW2 alternates a track's adjacent clips of different media over two composition tracks and re-measures. (b) rebuild ≤ 1.5 s and the apply ≤ 0.5 s, else the times go in the guide and a Performance-project candidate is filed (no proxies built). (c) the largest N with ≥ 98 % composed at Half is the viewer's live cell count: N ≥ 4 four live cells; 2–3 live up to N, rest refreshed on pause; < 2 every cell refreshed only when paused or after a switch. (d) record only.

spikes.question: Does mouth movement from Vision face landmarks (VNDetectFaceLandmarksRequest rev 3, 76-point inner lips, 10 samples/s per 1080p angle) tell who is talking on a one-mic, two-camera conversation, and how fast? Runs before SW8 on S-POD-1MIC, truth from S-POD-2CAM's two-mic switch.
spikes.rule: ≥ 85 % agreement on single-speaker speech seconds and ≥ 4× realtime per angle → SW8 built as SW-81; 70–85 % → built with SW-82's hedge and a 3 s minimum shot; < 70 % → SW8 not built, a candidate issue records the numbers.

spikes.question: What bleed margin, dominance, minimum turn and lead make the switch right on real speech? Runs inside SW2 on F-TURNS (bleed −12/−18/−24 dB, floors −55/−45 dBFS) and a 5-minute excerpt of S-POD-2CAM, truth on unambiguous steps (one mic's ℓ − P exceeds the other's by 20 dB).
spikes.rule: Defaults are the values that place every synthetic cut within one frame and maximise agreement on the excerpt. SW2 ships them when the excerpt agrees on ≥ 90 % of unambiguous seconds with no silent-listener shot of min_shot or longer; otherwise SW2 ships with the sheet's bleed row shown by default, the guide naming the case and the numbers recorded.

shared_needs: A video-analysis lane and per-media Vision cache separate from MediaCacheLane's width-2 audio lane (faces with tracking ids and inner-lip landmarks at 10 samples/s): SW8 needs the lips, VR the face/person rectangles, CO the person masks — one CJ infrastructure phase

AudioSourceKey (media, stream, channel) from SW4: every bet reading per-media audio caches (TX transcripts, FC loudness and laughter, CO hide-camera-while-silent reading the mic's speech) should read through it once SW4 lands

Link groups replace format 28's linked and every AP9 rule; AP9's proof re-runs whole, one mutant per rule
